AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Domestic Hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Domestic Hygiene.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Domestic Hygiene.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Domestic Hygiene.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Domestic Hygiene.

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals.

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Fruits.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Fruits.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Fruits.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Fruits.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Wild Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Wild Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Wild Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Wild Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Wild Animals.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food food frying food? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food food frying food.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food food frying food.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food food frying food.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food food frying food.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Balanced Meal and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking Food food frying food and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Personal Hygiene and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Domestic Hygiene and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Domestic Hygiene.

2. A — Ice melting to water

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.

9. A — Producers

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Fruits.

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Wild Animals.

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food food frying food.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Balanced Meal; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Personal Hygiene; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Domestic Hygiene; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
